svg.title: Three-step progressive correction of a flawed test item
svg.desc: Diagram illustrating the three-step revision of a flawed classroom test item, removing negative phrasing, eliminating grammatical clues, and replacing implausible distractors with diagnostic alternatives.

g.text: Stem: "Which of the following is NOT an un-important organ in the body that does NOT pump blood?"
Options: A) heart, B) brain, C) an kidney, D) None of the above.
Violations: Convoluted triple negative; grammatical clue 'an'; forbidden non-functional foil.
Stem: "Which organ is responsible for pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues?"
Options: A) Heart, B) Brain, C) Kidney, D) Lungs.
Improvements: Positive problem statement; grammatical parallel; eliminated clues & trick foils.
Stem: "A physician notes that oxygenated blood arriving from the lungs is not being delivered
effectively to systemic tissues. Which organ's muscular pumping function is directly impaired?"
A) Heart (Key); B) Lungs (Diagnoses gas exchange confusion); C) Kidney (Filtration confusion).
Elevation: Transforms rote recall into applied clinical problem solving with diagnostic foils.
Three-step item refinement: from raw draft to diagnostic assessment
Systematic sanitisation removes cognitive barriers and elevates questions to authentic application.
